newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta drifts around 83.40 zone against mark.
newsitem.headline: Peseta drifts around 83.40 zone against mark.

text.p: The peseta drifted in late trade on Friday after failing to make a clear break of the key 83.40 per mark zone, but remained firm thanks to weakness in the mark.
By 1730 GMT, the peseta was trading at 83.40/43 per mark, after touching 83.30 earlier in the session and compared with late Thursday levels of 83.48/49.
But traders did not rule out further appreciation if the mark continued to remain weak against the European crosses.
"It is possible that on Monday we could see 83.15 per mark," said one trader.
Yet traders also did not rule out the possibility of the Bank of Spain re-entering the market around the 83.00 per mark region.
"Below 83.00 the Bank of Spain may enter and the comments from de Molins this morning were a warning to the government that the CiU are not viewing the strength positively," one trader said.
Joaquin Molins, spokesman for Catalonia's CiU coalition, which gives key backing to the ruling party, told state radio that he was concerned about the economic impact of the peseta's recent strength.
